To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
parental overweight and low socio-economic status are the most important determinants of childhood obesity.
parental obesity is associated with an increased risk for obesity in children and adolescents.

parental overweight, low socio-economic status, maternal smoking, high birth weight, high weight gain in pregnancy, high meat and sausage consumption, high consumption of beverages and high energy intake are potential determinants of childhood obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comprehensive analysis of potential determinants of overweight and obesity among children and adolescent and their association with SES.
the identification of potential determinants of overweight and obesity among children and young people in Germany.
the question of how the prevalence of obesity can be lowered in children and adolescents in the long term.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more of the above listed determinants are present, the higher the risk of obesity.
the more risk factors a child or adolescent has, the higher the probability that he or she is obese.
obesity is a multifactorial problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a healthy lifestyle is important for children and adolescents of all SES, but it is even more important for children and adolescent with a low SES.
a combination of several factors is necessary for the development of obesity.
obesity prevention needs to address the whole family and should be targeted at children and adolescents from low socio-economic backgrounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many potential determinants of childhood obesity, and that the association of these factors with obesity is not uniform across the entire child population.
the risk of obesity is not evenly distributed in German children and adolescents, and that the risk of developing obesity is increased for children and adolescents from families with low SES.
the most effective prevention strategies should be tailored to the individual child or adolescent and their parents, and should take the family's socio-economic status into account.
